Additional mechanisms contribute to cancer risk with alcohol consumption. It is thought that heavy alcohol consumption can cause a decrease in [folic acid](/wiki/Folate "Folate") availability which can decrease the availability of nucleotides for DNA repair.[[8]](#cite_note-Varela-Rey_2013b-8) Additionally ethanol can decrease the conversion of homocysteine to methionine which is an essential amino acid that is part of the formation of SAMe.[[8]](#cite_note-Varela-Rey_2013b-8)[[27]](#cite_note-Purohita3-27)

Increased inflammation due to alcohol consumption can increase various cytokine formations especially [NF-κB](/wiki/NF-%CE%BAB "NF-κB") which is a transcription factor.[[9]](#cite_note-Rumgay_2021b-9)

Additionally alcohol usage is associated with lower Vitamin A levels which causes a reduction in [retinoid](/wiki/Retinoid "Retinoid") conversion and signaling.[[9]](#cite_note-Rumgay_2021b-9)[[25]](#cite_note-Pöschl_2004-25)[[27]](#cite_note-Purohita3-27)

Individuals who both smoke and drink are at a much higher risk of developing mouth, tracheal, and esophageal cancer. Ethanol is thought to potentially be a solvent for carcinogenic factors in smoking.[[29]](#cite_note-Boffetta_2006-29) Research has shown their risk of developing these cancers is 35 times higher than in individuals who neither smoke nor drink. This evidence may suggest that there is a cocarcinogenic interaction between alcohol and tobacco-related carcinogens.[[31]](#cite_note-aa213-31)[[32]](#cite_note-cancerres.aacrjournals.org-32)

The **vice premiers of the State Council of the People's Republic of China** serves as a deputy leader within the [State Council](/wiki/State_Council_of_the_PRC "State Council of the PRC"). In terms of administrative hierarchy, the Vice Premier holds a position superior to that of [ministers](/wiki/Ministries_of_the_People%27s_Republic_of_China "Ministries of the People's Republic of China"), commission directors, and the [Secretary-General of the State Council](/wiki/Secretary-General_of_the_State_Council "Secretary-General of the State Council"), while remaining subordinate to the Premier and holding a rank equivalent to that of [State Councilors](/wiki/State_Councilor "State Councilor").[[1]](#cite_note-organic_law-1) Generally, the title is held by multiple individuals at any given time, with each vice-premier holding a broad portfolio of responsibilities. The first vice-premier takes over duties of the premier at the time of the latter's incapacity. The incumbent vice premiers, in order of rank, are [Ding Xuexiang](/wiki/Ding_Xuexiang "Ding Xuexiang"), [He Lifeng](/wiki/He_Lifeng "He Lifeng"), [Zhang Guoqing](/wiki/Zhang_Guoqing "Zhang Guoqing") and [Liu Guozhong](/wiki/Liu_Guozhong "Liu Guozhong").

The highest-ranked office holder is informally called the **Senior Vice Premier** or **First Vice Premier** ([Chinese](/wiki/Simplified_Chinese_characters "Simplified Chinese characters"): 第一副总理) or **Executive Vice Premier** ([Chinese](/wiki/Simplified_Chinese_characters "Simplified Chinese characters"): 常务副总理), a most prominent case being [Deng Xiaoping](/wiki/Deng_Xiaoping "Deng Xiaoping") in the mid-to-late 1970s.[[2]](#cite_note-nas_gov_sg-2)[[3]](#cite_note-Xia_Shen_2014_pp._1083–1113-3) In irregular instances, the position of a senior vice premier has been named either to indicate degree of power, nominal power, or when the premier is incapacitated and requires a full-time deputy to carry out his regular duties.

[Julius Erving](/wiki/Julius_Erving "Julius Erving") played 11 seasons with the 76ers from 1976 to 1987, leading the 76ers to four NBA Finals and ultimately winning an NBA championship in 1983.

The 76ers finally came all the way back in 1976–77, in large part due to the [ABA–NBA merger](/wiki/ABA%E2%80%93NBA_merger "ABA–NBA merger"). The ABA's last champions, the [New York Nets](/wiki/New_York_Nets "New York Nets"), were facing a burden of $5 million to the Knicks for entering the [New York metropolitan area](/wiki/New_York_metropolitan_area "New York metropolitan area") on top of the $3.2 million expansion fee for joining the NBA. So, when the 76ers offered to buy the contract of the Nets' franchise player, [Julius Erving](/wiki/Julius_Erving "Julius Erving"), for $3 million—roughly the cost of NBA membership—the Nets had little choice but to accept.
